title: Split a String in Balanced Strings
summary: A balanced string consists of an equal number of 'L' and 'R' characters.
statement: A balanced string consists of an equal number of 'L' and 'R' characters. Given a balanced string s, determine the greatest number of balanced substrings that can be formed.
constraints: s has equal total counts of L and R.
Split into the maximum number of nonempty balanced substrings.
hints: Represent R as +1 and L as -1.
A prefix is balanced exactly when the running sum returns to zero.
Cut greedily at every zero and count those returns.
Any balanced piece must end at a zero; taking the earliest such end cannot reduce later opportunities.
editorial: Any balanced piece must end at a zero; taking the earliest such end cannot reduce later opportunities.

tests.explanation: The running balance returns to zero four times.
The earliest zero balances create three substrings.
